title: State (NCT of Delhi) v. Navjot Sandhu @ Afshan Guru & Ors. (Parliament Attack Case)
crime_type: Attack on Democratic Parliament / Waging War / Falsified Vehicle Movement
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Delhi
source: Supreme Court of India Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1359141)
ipc_sections: Section 121 IPC (Waging war against the Government of India)
location: Parliament House Complex, New Delhi, India
evidence: White Ambassador car bearing counterfeit Home Ministry VIP security parking stickers and fake sirens
Five AK-47 rifles, grenade launchers, satellite phone equipment, and unexploded ammonium nitrate car bomb recovered on premise
Call Detail Records (CDR) matching mobile handsets seized from terrorists to Afzal Guru operational numbers
Laptop computer recovered with forged identity card templates and Parliament layout schematics
modus_operandi: Procured a second-hand Ambassador vehicle, fitted it with counterfeit Ministry of Home Affairs VIP entry passes, flashing beacons, and packed boot with explosives. Breached Parliament gates while legislature was in session, opening indiscriminate automatic fire when challenged by security personnel.
personality_disorder: Systematic political radicalization, surreptitious logistical deceit, and willingness to enable catastrophic violence.
common_traits: Impersonation of government VIP convoys using fake passes
Direct kinetic assault on democratic constitutional institutions
Mobile handset synchronization through compartmentalized handlers
Use of ammonium nitrate and RDX fuel-air mixtures
summary: The 2001 Indian Parliament attack brought India and Pakistan to the brink of military conflict. Supreme Court upheld the capital conviction of Afzal Guru under Section 121 and 302, reaffirming jurisprudence on intercepted telecom surveillance in terror conspiracies.
